newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money rises, mkt tightens at month-end.
newsitem.headline: German call money rises, mkt tightens at month-end.

text.p: German call money rose to 3.10/15 percent on Thursday from 3.00/05 on Wednesday as the market tightened ahead of the month-end.
Dealers said money taken up until the start of the new month was already changing hands at rates of over four percent and predicted a further rise in call money rates this week.
"Those who need more money to meet minimum reserve requirements are making provisions today, to avoid having to pay four percent or even the Lombard rate (of 4.50) tomorrow," one trader said.
One trader estimated that one or two billion marks was likely to be borrowed from the Bundesbank at the Lombard rate on Friday.

Banks' reserve holdings at the central bank totalled 41.5 billion marks on Wednesday after 40.8 billion on Tuesday. The average for the month was 39.4 billion for the first 27 days, up slightly from 39.3 billion the previous day.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average FIONA= was set at 3.04300 percent on Thursday compared with 3.05350 percent on Wednesday.
